D4: GitHub repo defisaver/defisaver-v3-contracts identified from website footer. mainnet.json fetched from main branch (not pinned SHA — branch pointer only; SHA unavailable from GitHub UI render). 29+ named contracts extracted with addresses. Arbitrum/Optimism/Base JSON files exist at addresses/ directory but not fetched this run due to budget constraints.

D5: protocol.chains includes Arbitrum, Optimism, Base in addition to Ethereum. Docs confirm arbitrum.json, optimism.json, base.json exist in the GitHub repo. Not fetched this run. Recorded in unknowns.

D6: DFSRegistry (0x287778F121F134C66212FB16c9b53eC991D32f5b) is the primary factory/registry for protocol contracts — getAddr(id) enumerates all registered addresses. Not queried this run via read API. StrategyStorage, BundleStorage, SubStorage are storage registries for strategies/subscriptions. Factory enumeration deferred to next run.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: DFSRegistry=admin/registry; AdminVault=admin; RecipeExecutor=router; StrategyExecutor=router; ProxyAuth/SafeModuleAuth=other (auth); SubStorage/StrategyStorage/BundleStorage=other (storage); BotAuth=guardian; FeeRecipient/FeeReceiver=treasury; WrapperExchangeRegistry/ExchangeAggregatorRegistry=other (allowlist); ZrxAllowlist=other (allowlist); DFSProxyRegistry=other (user proxy registry). Owner/multisig addresses not yet surfaced from on-chain reads.

D8: All 29 admin_addresses entries trace to the fetched mainnet.json GitHub page. The audit-era REGISTRY_ADDR (0xB0e1682D17A96E8551191c089673346dF7e1D467) traces to the ConsenSys audit page. No fabricated addresses used.

Confirms: DFSRegistry owned by multisig; core contracts 7-day timelock, strategy action contracts 1-day timelock. Automation upgrades use 2/3 multisig (Admin) for timelock activation and 3/5 multisig (Owner) for initiating upgrades. RecipeExecutor owned by multisig (can kill or withdraw). ProxyAuth and SafeModuleAuth are immutable auth contracts.

protocol_metadata.about: DeFi Saver is a non-custodial DeFi management dashboard that lets users create, manage, and automate leveraged or collateralized positions across protocols such as Aave, MakerDAO, Spark, Compound, Morpho, and others. Users interact via DSProxy or Safe smart wallets, executing composable 'recipes' (multi-action transactions) and configuring automated strategies (e.g., stop-loss, take-profit, leverage boost/repay) that bots execute trustlessly on their behalf. The core protocol contracts are mostly immutable logic contracts whose addresses are registered in the DFSRegistry — itself upgradeable by a multisig with configurable timelocks (7 days for core contracts, 1 day for strategy action contracts). Automation upgrades require a 3-of-5 Owner multisig to initiate and a 2-of-3 Admin multisig to unlock the 24-hour timelock.
